newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie tottering after break to 16-mth low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie tottering after break to 16-mth low.

text.p: *AUD looking vulnerable after finally breaking the range floor overnight in an impulsive stop loss move to a 16-month low
*European and exporter bids saw $0.7550 re-taken, but bounce modest at best and upside thick with US/Japanese bank offers
*Charts point to test of $0.7490/7500 support next
*May jobs data at 11.30 am may help clarify rate outlook
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the dollar was poised precariously at US0.7558/63 having slipped from US$0.7595/00 late here Tuesday.

Dealers said the repeated rejection at US$0.7630 resistance earlier in the week had undermined sentiment while heavy selling of AUD/yen out of Tokyo had applied pressure from a new direction. This left support too weakened to survive persistent offers from the Chicago IMM overnight.

Some dealers said a report from Access Economics suggesting interest rates could fall further if growth failed to match RBA expectations also played a part in the slide. Why investors should react to such an obvious statement was not clear.
The Reserve Bank's bold easing last month showed just how confident it was about inflation remaining low and how concerned it had become about stubbornly high unemployment.

"It doesn't take a genius to work out that the bank will cut again if the economy doesn't show signs of responding to past easings," said one dealer. "It obviously believes there's enough spare capacity for the economy to run at four percent or more and will do everything possible to ensure that."
Whether further policy action would be needed might be a little clearer after today's jobs data, although a result in line with forecasts would leave the market no wiser.

Median estimates are for employment to rise 15,000 following a April's 37,100 gain. Monthly jobs growth at that level would only be enough to keep the jobless rate stable at 8.7 percent, a level the RBA has often expressed disappointment at.

The risks for the currency with this figure look all on the downside since it would take a rise well above the top forecast of 25,000 to calm investor fears over rates. In contrast any outcome like the lowest prediction of a 5,000 fall would have the money market slavering for an immediate easing.
The A$ remained weak on the yen at 84.10/20 having slumped 1-1/2 big figures Tuesday to 84.20/30. -- Wayne Cole 9373 1800
